summary: It is an interactive, web-based 3D Space Mission Design Game built with Three.js that transforms complex aerospace engineering into an accessible, physics-driven simulation. Addressing the challenge of engaging users in authentic mission planning, the platform guides players through four realistic mission phases: Spacecraft & Payload Configuration, Orbital Transfer & Aerobraking, Entry, Descent, and Landing (EDL), and Autonomous Rover Surface Operations.Instead of arbitrary arcade mechanics, every stage is governed by real astrophysical equations and empirical NASA planetary datasets. Players must balance mass budgets, calculate $\Delta v$ requirements using the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, manage atmospheric drag during descent, and optimize autonomous rover paths using the A* pathfinding algorithm under solar energy constraints. By combining real-time 3D visualization with deterministic physics, AstroNova bridges the gap between theoretical orbital mechanics and hands-on engineering decision-making for students, educators, and space enthusiasts worldwide.
details:
Overview & How It Works

It is a browser-based 3D space mission simulator that lets users design, launch, and operate an interplanetary mission from scratch. The simulation is structured into four sequential engineering phases:

  1. Spacecraft & Payload Design: Users select propulsion systems, fuel capacities, thermal shields, and scientific payloads while monitoring total wet/dry mass ratios and $\Delta v$ budgets in real time.
  2. Interplanetary Transfer & Orbit Insertion: Powered by orbital mechanics, users execute Hohmann transfer trajectories and manage fuel consumption to achieve stable target orbits.
  3. Entry, Descent, and Landing (EDL): The simulation calculates real-time atmospheric drag ($F_d = \frac{1}{2}\rho v^2 C_d A$) based on target planetary atmospheric density profiles, requiring precise timing for heat shield protection and parachute deployment.
  4. Autonomous Rover Surface Operations: Once landed, users deploy a planetary rover across terrain maps containing crater hazards and elevation gradients. An integrated A* pathfinding algorithm computes optimal navigation routes by balancing terrain traversal costs against solar power generation and battery budgets.

Technology Stack & Architecture

  • 3D Rendering & Physics Engine: Three.js, JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, CSS3.
  • Data Architecture: To ensure zero-latency performance and 60 FPS rendering within the browser's requestAnimationFrame loop, empirical parameters from NASA planetary datasets were normalized into modular, lightweight JSON configuration objects.
  • Algorithms: Tsiolkovsky Rocket Equation, Newtonian orbital kinematics, aerodynamic drag modeling, and A* heuristic pathfinding.

Impact & Creativity

Traditional mission design tools require steep learning curves and specialized desktop software. AstroNova democratizes aerospace systems engineering by making trade-off analysis (mass vs. fuel vs. science return) visually intuitive and immediately playable on any web browser without installation.
